subject: SLO Elevation & Support Rollout — Atlas Robotics renewal checklist
messages:
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@atlas-robotics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlas-robotics.com
Date: 2026-12-13T15:21:00Z
Subject: Renewal questions — SLO uplift and support tier

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Atlas is preparing the renewal packet and leadership is strongly in favor of moving to a higher SLO band and a priority support tier for 2027. A few specifics they asked us to confirm: 

- Can Redwood commit to a 99.8% availability SLO with a 95th/99th latency target of <120ms / <300ms for our production traffic?
- We expect a 35% increase in Q1 token throughput (see attached projection). Can you outline how dedicated capacity + burst would be structured and what the lead times are?
- Procurement will need a clear Appendix to attach to the PO with the uplifted SLA and support response times.

We are happy to proceed if we have clear timelines and an updated pricing delta. Procurement included on cc — they will handle the PO once legal and SRE align.

Best,
Sam
Director of Platform
Atlas Robotics

[Attachment: capacity_projection_Q1-27.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@atlas-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, procurement@atlas-robotics.com
Date: 2026-12-13T20:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — SLO uplift and support tier

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the projection. Internal thread below for context. Quick answers up front: we can support the uplift you propose with a Premium SLO addendum, a dedicated capacity reservation pattern plus burst, and a staged rollout to hit the latency targets while limiting risk.

Attached: a draft SLA appendix and a proposed rollout timeline (MAD = Monitor, Adjust, Deploy). Pricing delta and contract language are noted in the appendix.

Proposed next steps (high level):
1) Technical readiness call (SREs) — this week to confirm traffic patterns and warmup plan.
2) Legal: sign SLA appendix and PO terms — we can fast-track a single addendum.
3) Ops: schedule a staged capacity ramp with a one-week canary and automatic fallback to the current model if tail latencies exceed thresholds.

Tentative timeline:
- Dec 14–16: SRE deep-dive & finalize appendix language
- Dec 17: DocuSign to procurement for signature
- Jan 4–10: capacity reservation provisioning & canary
- Jan 11: full cutover to elevated SLOs (assuming canary success)

I’ve looped Marissa and Ben for pricing and operational sign-off. See attachments.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Appendix_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: MAD_rollout_timeline.pptx (pptx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — SLO uplift and support tier

Priya / all — solid plan. A couple of operational clarifications and a small ask from Legal:

Operational clarifications:
- The 99.8% availability SLO is achievable if Atlas takes a reserved capacity tier + a 20% warm-burst buffer for the first 30 days of the cutover. We should call this out explicitly in the appendix so procurement understands committed capacity vs. burstable capacity.
- For latency targets, we recommend a two-stage latency acceptance window: the canary week with 95th < 140ms and 99th < 350ms, then full acceptance at the tighter targets you listed. That gives us room to tune quantization/kv cache warming.

Legal ask / contracting note:
- Legal requests an explicit rollback clause and an SLO measurement methodology (which logs, which region replication, and how downtime is computed). I’ve added a paragraph to SLA_Appendix_v1.pdf — see highlighted notes.

Pricing / credits:
- Ben, can you confirm the monthly uplift estimate and whether we can offer a one-time onramp credit for any provisioning inefficiencies? I suggest a small operational credit to smooth the renewal.

I’ll be available for the SRE call this afternoon.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal questions — SLO uplift and support tier

Thanks everyone — quick pricing and procurement notes.

Pricing delta (high level):
- Reserved capacity tier (baseline): +28% on current committed spend
- Warm-burst buffer (first 30 days): one-time charge equal to 5% of a monthly commit
- Premium SLO Appendix (includes priority support & SLA credits): +9% on top of reserved tier

Net uplift: ~+37% month-over-month on committed baseline (estimates in capacity_projection_Q1-27.xlsx). I’ve added a one-time onramp credit equal to the warm-burst charge; that will make the first month neutral on one-time provisioning fees.

Procurement steps for Atlas:
1) We will send the SLA Appendix via DocuSign (link below). Please confirm signers on your side.
2) Once signed, procurement should issue a PO referencing DEAL-ATLAS-2026-11.
3) Engineering will start provisioning upon receipt of the signed addendum and PO — we expect 5 business days for dedicated pool allocation after signatures are in.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/atlas-sla-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654321/DEAL-ATLAS-2026-11

Sam — if procurement confirms a signer and timeline today we can get the DocuSign out before COB and begin provisioning next week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
